 Mishara ton powers Chitwan Rhinos into Qualifier 2
 TRN Online 
 Thu, 19 November 2026 
 Share 
 Change Font Sizes: 
 TRN Online 
 Share: 
 Thu, 19 November 2026 
 By Pramod Joshi 
 Kirtipur, Nov. 19:  Kamil Mishara produced a record-breaking century as Chitwan Rhinos thrashed Kathmandu Gorkhas by 61 runs on Wednesday to book a place in Qualifier 2 of the Nepal Premier League (NPL) Season 3.
 The victory sets up a Qualifier 2 clash with Sudurpaschim Royals on 19 November, with a place in the final at stake.
 For Kathmandu, it was another disappointing playoff exit. After missing the playoffs in the inaugural season and falling in the Eliminator last year, the Gorkhas once again saw their title hopes end before the final.
 Chitwan, meanwhile, reached Qualifier 2 for the first time. They were eliminated in the Eliminator by Karnali Yaks in Season 1 and failed to qualify for the playoffs in Season 2.
 Opting to bat first at the TU Cricket Ground, Chitwan piled up 204/4, riding on an unbeaten century from Mishara and a half-century from captain Ravi Bopara.
 Kathmandu never seriously threatened the target and finished on 143/9 from their 20 overs.
 The chase was derailed by Chitwan bowler duo Rijan Dhakal and Pakistan leg-spinner Usama Mir, who shared seven wickets between them. 
 Dhakal starred with outstanding figures of 4/16, taking his tally to a tournament-leading 15 wickets. Mir provided excellent support with 3/15.
 Dhakal struck twice early, removing Shail Patel (2) and Sam Heazlett (3) to leave Kathmandu struggling at 30/2.
 William Bosisto attempted a fightback with 37 off 28 balls, including three fours and two sixes, while Sri Lankan Sahan Arachchige added a brisk 24 from 13 deliveries. Rashid Khan chipped in with 12, but wickets continued to tumble at regular intervals.
 Captain Karan KC (1), Jahandad Khan (1) and Sonu Devkota (6) failed to make an impact, while Santosh Yadav contributed 10. 
 Bhim Sharki remained unbeaten on 30 from 17 balls, striking three sixes, but the target was well beyond Kathmandu's reach.
 After being knocked out, Kathmandu skipper KC said a missed opportunity in the field ultimately proved decisive. He felt the dropped catch offered to Kamil Mishara by William Bosisto shifted the momentum firmly in Chitwan's favour. 
 KC also acknowledged that Kathmandu's fielding fell short of expectations and stressed the need for improvement despite an otherwise encouraging campaign.
 Mishara shines 
 Earlier, Chitwan recovered superbly after losing Dev Khanal (17) and Dawid Malan (0) in successive deliveries from Karan KC in the fourth over.
 The setback only brought together the match-defining partnership. Mishara and Bopara added 154 runs for the third wicket, the second-highest partnership in NPL history, laying the foundation for a commanding total.
 Mishara stole the show with a breathtaking unbeaten 120 from 59 balls, smashing 10 sixes and five fours. 
 His knock is now the highest individual score in NPL history, surpassing Mark Watt's unbeaten 114 for Karnali Yaks against Lumbini Lions last season. 
 The Sri Lankan reached his century in just 53 balls and became only the second centurion of the current season after Pokhara Avengers' Yuvraj Samra.
 Bopara marked his 500th career appearance with an influential 53 from 42 balls, striking three fours and two sixes before being bowled by Rashid Khan. The Englishman's second fifty of the tournaments moved him to third on the season's run-scoring charts with 237 runs.
 Bibek Yadav added eight before falling to Rashid, while Karan KC and Rashid Khan claimed two wickets apiece for Kathmandu.
 Defending champions Lumbini Lions have already secured their place in the final after defeating Sudurpaschim Royals by six wickets in Qualifier 1. 
 Chitwan will now aim to continue their momentum when they face Sudurpaschim for a maiden berth in the NPL final.
 Chitwan captain Ravi Bopara lauded Kamil Mishara for his match-winning century and said the team's confidence would be key heading into Qualifier 2. 
 Bopara expressed pride in his side's performance and belief that the Rhinos could build on the momentum despite having little turnaround time between matches. 
 He added that going straight into another knockout fixture with confidence running high could work in Chitwan's favour.
